project_scope.note: Central Texas green-hemiparasite reference module. Castilleja lindheimeri is now the canonical clickable local paintbrush anchor; Joey Y7A530PjEbU provides private-study habitat/hemiparasite context.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: First recognize that many local members are fully green hemiparasites. Then inspect the bracted spike, fused bilateral corolla, superior ovary, and many-seeded capsule.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Simple and exstipulate; opposite or alternate depending on genus.
family_diagnostics.flower: Fused tubular usually zygomorphic corolla, commonly 4 stamens.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Do not uproot plants to prove parasitism; haustoria are underground.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Orobanchaceae is a good anti-stereotype family: many local members are green, leafy, and photosynthetic even though they are root hemiparasites.

steps.title: 1 · See a green hemiparasite
steps.look_for: A normal-looking green herb with a bracted flowering axis.
steps.why_it_matters: Breaks the 'parasitic plant = pale leafless thing' misconception.

steps.title: 2 · Read the flower tube
steps.look_for: Fused, usually zygomorphic corolla with about 4 fertile stamens.
steps.why_it_matters: Places the family among other tubular-flowered Lamiales.

steps.title: 3 · Look at the bracts
steps.look_for: In paintbrushes, much of the bright orange-red/scarlet display is a set of floral bracts surrounding much less conspicuous tubular flowers.
steps.why_it_matters: The local Castilleja anchor prevents the common mistake of calling the colorful bracts 'petals.'

steps.title: 4 · Confirm the capsule
steps.look_for: A dry capsule with numerous tiny seeds.
steps.why_it_matters: Helps separate the family from Lamiaceae nutlets.

comparisons.title: Orobanchaceae vs Plantaginaceae
comparisons.rule: Corolla shape can overlap. Orobanchaceae adds parasitic biology and often strongly bracted inflorescences; both may have capsules.

comparisons.title: Orobanchaceae vs Lamiaceae
comparisons.rule: Lamiaceae commonly has a deeply 4-lobed ovary and four nutlets; Orobanchaceae commonly has a many-seeded capsule.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not uproot plants to verify parasitism, and do not assume all family members are achlorophyllous.

castilleja_training_module.title: Paintbrush anatomy: the colored brush is not one big flower
castilleja_training_module.look_here_first: Use a side-on Castilleja spike. Find the colored floral BRACT below a flower, the colored CALYX surrounding its base, and then the narrower projecting COROLLA. This gives learners a concrete way to understand a bracted Orobanchaceae inflorescence before they compare species.
teaching_points: Castilleja is a green root hemiparasite: it photosynthesizes but also forms underground haustorial connections to host roots.
The conspicuous red, orange, pink, or purple display is largely bract/calyx tissue; the true flower is the narrower bilateral corolla.
Family confirmation should include a fused bilateral corolla and eventually a dry many-seeded capsule; do not treat color as a family character.
Do not uproot plants merely to demonstrate parasitism.
